title: git: Add test cases
description:
Add git dissection test cases to existing testing suite for: finding git
packets, finding the Git Protocol version, finding the right amount of
Flush and Delimiter packets, not finding Malformed packets.

Oh, I misunderstood when I read this the first time!

So in this test we're asserting that there are *not* any malformed packets, right?

At very least, I think the description is misleading - since you use "Check if blah exists" everywhere else where you're expecting it to exist, but here you're using "Check if blah exists" but checking that it *does not* exist. I wonder whether your descriptions overall could be more opinionated - that is, instead of "Check if there's Git delim packets", you could say, "Ensure that Git delim packets are parsed"; and for this test, you could say, "Ensure that no packets are incorrectly marked as malformed".

But really, I don't think this is a compelling test case, now that I read it again. Maybe someone else disagrees with me. I don't find "Check that some random Git pcap doesn't have any malformed packets in it" to be that interesting.

If you want a regression test to say "delim packets aren't misinterpreted as malformed packets", then fine, but I'd say you should check both conditions in the same test - that is, "pcap foo contains delim packets *and* pcap foo does not contain malformed packets", and describe the test accordingly as a regression test.

The previous three tests all cover the same dissection results. I would suggest combining these tests into one.

Use multiple `-e` options and check the tab-separated fields. See the `test_tcp_out_of_order_first_gap` test in the same file for an example.

The first test could be removed if you use the `-Y git` option, it is a display filter that will have no results if there are no Git packets.

The disadvantage is that it can make it a little slower to track down what failed if the test failed, but I think the advantages outweigh the disadvantage here.

+@fixtures.mark_usefixtures('test_env')
+@fixtures.uses_fixtures
+class case_dissect_git(subprocesstest.SubprocessTestCase):
+    def test_git_prot(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, features):
+        '''
+        Check for Git protocol version 2, flush and delimiter packets.
+        Ensure there are no malformed packets.
+        '''
+        proc = self.assertRun((cmd_tshark,
+                '-r', capture_file('gitOverTCP.pcap'),
+                '-Ygit', '-Tfields', '-egit.version', '-egit.packet_type',
+                '-zexpert', '-e_ws.expert',
+            ))
+        # `epan/dissectors/packet-git.c` parses the Git Protocol version
+        # from ASCII '1' or '2' to integers 49 or 50 in grep output.
+        # 0x0000 are flush packets.
+        # 0x0001 are delimiter packets.
+        # Pre-existing git Malformed Packets in this pcap were addressed
+        # with the parsing of the delimiter packets. This test ensures
+        # pcap gitOverTCP's delim packets are parsed and that there are no
+        # malformed packets with "Expert Info/Errors" in the same pcap.
+        # Additional test cases for other scenarios, i.e actually malformed
+        # git packets, might be required.
+        self.assertEqual(proc.stdout_str, '50\t\t\n\t0\t\n\t\t\n\t1,0\t\n')
